posture_summary.text: Latvia stands as one of NATO's most exposed and institutionally integrated frontline states, having undergone the most rapid security transformation in Europe since Russia's 2022 invasion. The country of 1.8 million people is spending nearly 5% of GDP on defense while hosting a 3,500-strong multinational NATO brigade and developing comprehensive border defense contingencies, yet faces a demographic death spiral having lost 30% of its population since 1990. Latvia has achieved maximum institutional lock-in across Western frameworks with zero hedging toward alternative powers, making defection structurally impossible without state collapse. The society remains internally fractured along ethnic lines with 25-30% Russian-speaking population increasingly marginalized through language and citizenship policies, while coalition governments exhibit chronic instability with 17 prime ministers in 33 years. Latvia's strategic culture, forged by occupation memory and deportation trauma, produces extraordinary alliance commitment but operates under mounting fiscal and demographic pressures.
